model: T410A and T410B line voltage electric heat thermostats (do-it-yourself models)
notes: Line-voltage thermostat for radiant cable, electric baseboard and resistive-rated fan-forced heaters, rated 22 A at 120 to 240 Vac and 19 A at 277 Vac for 60 Hz noninductive loads (Resideo's product data calls it a resistive rating). The T410A breaks one line and the T410B breaks both.

gaps: The copy read is revision 69-1562-1 (2002); Resideo's later 69-1562-02 sheet and product data 68-0145EF-02 give the same ratings and temperature range.
The 2002 instructions name a sensing element without saying what it is, so none is claimed; the product data lists a bimetal element and a snap-acting switch, not added as parts.
The mercury notice is about the old control being replaced; it does not say the T410 contains mercury, so no mercury is claimed.
No production years, SKUs or circuit board are given, and no teardown was found.
The 277 V (19 A) rating is in the spec but not in the volts field, which holds the 120 to 240 V range.
method: Honeywell T410A,B installation instructions 69-1562-1 (copyright 2002 Honeywell, Honeywell address and form number on pages 1 and 4), copy on morelectricheating.com; pages 1 to 4 read.
Resideo-hosted 69-1562-02 install sheet and product data 68-0145EF-02 read for comparison; the product data is cited for the resistive wording.
Not used: the Cadet T521 line-voltage model; only its ratings were readable on manualslib.

comps.spec: Line-voltage electric heat thermostat: 22 A at 120 to 240 Vac and 19 A at 277 Vac, 60 Hz noninductive loads; temperature range 40 to 80 F. T410A has a single-line break, T410B a double-line break
Switch that clicks as it makes and breaks contact when the setting knob is turned (check-out steps); T410A breaks one line, T410B breaks both
